account:
Today seems mostly routine, though the town's financial records are missing from the places we checked. The secretary found no accounts or bills in the great hall chests, and I found 128 emeralds but no records in the treasury. I left the funds untouched. I do not know where the accounts are; this alone does not establish wrongdoing.

The builder has been seeking repair instructions and payment terms. I requested inspections and an itemized estimate, with urgent hazards reported promptly, and approved no repair spending. Tonight the builder came near my home and reported no confirmed damage on the bridge or the east-bank routes walked, lanterns present, and no expenditure. The remaining west-bank roads are to be inspected tomorrow. My acknowledgment was not heard, so I should not assume the builder received my further request for written findings.

The neighbour reported no damage, ordinary baking glow, a quiet warehouse, and an available ferry. The baker offered advance bread orders and the innkeeper asked about expected visitors. I know of no planned gathering or visitors and requested no town bread order; these inquiries appear to be ordinary business planning. I heard indistinct freight and builder conversations earlier, but cannot infer their contents.

I kept afternoon office hours and returned home for nineteen hundred. The secretary is keeping the appointment book ready for tomorrow morning. I should read it at the office; tomorrow's known appointments include the ten o'clock mill grain inspection.
